sum.dish: Pork-bone gamjatang stew — the house specialty since the shop opened in 1983.
sum.vibe: Old-school local institution that survived Seongsu's factory-to-hip transformation.
sum.wait: Wait times not verified yet — big local following, so peak meal hours get busy.
sum.tip: One of the longest-running restaurants in the area; a safe pick for a first taste of gamjatang.

sum.dish: Coffee and brunch plates inside a converted red-brick warehouse.
sum.vibe: The symbol of Seongsu's factory-renovation cafe scene — part gallery, part cafe, huge ceilings.
sum.wait: Wait times not verified yet — weekend afternoons are the busiest window.
sum.tip: Come for the space as much as the menu; art installations rotate through the hall.

sum.dish: Water-parsley (minari) dishes — fresh, green, and hard to find done this well elsewhere.
sum.vibe: Clean modern-Korean spot; its Yongsan sibling has appeared in the Michelin Guide.
sum.tip: Minari is the point — order whatever puts it front and center.

sum.dish: Fajita sets are the crowd favorite, per local guides.
sum.vibe: Lively K-Mexican spot in the Yeonmujang-gil alleys — good for groups who want drinks with dinner.
sum.tip: Mexican in Seoul runs Korean-spicy; ask for heat levels if you're sensitive.

sum.dish: Aged pork bulgogi and galbi grilled over charcoal.
sum.vibe: Smoky, meat-first K-BBQ energy north of Seongsu station.
sum.wait: Wait times not verified yet — BBQ spots here peak 7–9pm.
sum.tip: Aged pork (숙성) is the differentiator versus a standard samgyeopsal joint.

sum.dish: Handmade burgers with playful specials — the shrimp burger and fried button mushrooms get named repeatedly.
sum.vibe: Small indie burger shop loved by Seongsu office workers.
sum.wait: Wait times not verified yet — lunch rush is the pinch point.
sum.tip: Local writers recommend going beyond the basic cheeseburger; the odd-sounding specials deliver.

sum.dish: Attic omurice and rosé pasta — comfort-food fusion at friendly prices.
sum.vibe: Cozy, casual, date-friendly without the price tag.
sum.tip: Good budget option when the trendy spots' queues are out of hand.

sum.dish: Rich-broth ramen with housemade karaage on the side.
sum.vibe: Counter-style Japanese ramen shop — quick, solo-friendly.
sum.tip: Ramen counters turn over fast even with a line; don't be scared off by a short queue.

sum.dish: House-brewed craft beers with rotating taps.
sum.vibe: Multi-floor brewery with indoor and outdoor lounges — one of Seongsu's signature night spots.
sum.wait: Wait times not verified yet — weekend evenings fill up.
sum.tip: Taprooms handle groups better than most Seongsu venues; a solid plan-B for 6+.

sum.dish: Crème brûlée French toast is the signature local guides call out.
sum.vibe: Bright bakery-cafe good for a slow morning before the crowds.
sum.tip: Bakery items sell through — earlier is better for the signature toast.

sum.dish: Rotating gelato and sorbet flavors made in-house.
sum.vibe: Tiny dessert stop — the standard 'one more thing' after dinner in the alleys.
sum.tip: Gelato is the easiest zero-language-barrier order in Seongsu: point and smile.

sum.dish: Karaage with a famously thin, crackly crust, plus okonomiyaki.
sum.vibe: Izakaya-style Japanese spot a Seongsu local ranked among their nine favorites.
sum.tip: Pairs naturally with a highball; treat it as dinner-plus-drinks rather than a quick meal.

sum.dish: Ganjjajang (black-bean noodles) with unusually thin noodles, and tangsuyuk.
sum.vibe: No-frills Korean-Chinese diner — where locals actually eat lunch.
sum.wait: Wait times not verified yet — office lunch rush 12–1pm.
sum.tip: Korean-Chinese food is its own genre; jjajang + tangsuyuk is the canonical first order.

sum.dish: Galmaegisal (pork skirt) grilled over briquettes, finished with kimchi-mari noodles.
sum.vibe: Classic charcoal-smoke Korean grill house on Yeonmujang-gil.
sum.wait: Wait times not verified yet — dinner peak applies.
sum.tip: Galmaegisal is the cut locals order here; don't default to samgyeopsal.

sum.dish: 15-day aged pork neck that a local reviewer described as melting in the mouth, with kokumi rice.
sum.vibe: Premium-leaning pork grill — one of Seongsu's best-known meat destinations.
sum.wait: Wait times not verified yet — widely known, so plan around peak hours.
sum.tip: This is the splurge pick among Seongsu pork spots; come hungry and unhurried.

sum.dish: Futomaki (fat rolls) a local writer described as ingredients unfolding in the mouth.
sum.vibe: Small, quiet roll specialist — a light-but-special lunch.
sum.tip: Small kitchens sell out; earlier lunch beats later lunch here.

sum.dish: Kimchi stew and rolled omelette, eaten with cheap cold beer.
sum.vibe: A 'ga-maek' — half corner-store, half pub. As local as Seongsu nightlife gets.
sum.tip: Ga-maek culture = grab drinks from the fridge, order snacks, pay simple. A real only-in-Korea experience.
